'''Jarugu Narasimha Moorthy''' (born 1964)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Academy of Sciences |url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL2010032 |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=fellows.ias.ac.in}}</ref> is an Indian organic photochemist and former [[Director (education)|Director]] of [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram]]. He was a Dr. Jag Mohan Garg Chair Professor at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]].<ref name="Professor, Department of Chemistry">{{Cite web |url=http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/ |title=Professor, Department of Chemistry |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur}}</ref> He is known for his studies on organic photochemistry and supramolecular chemistry.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=365 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>  He is an elected fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/jnm.html |title=Faculty profile |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-date=20 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520130140/http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/jnm.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Moorthy,_Prof._Jarugu_Narasimha |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2008, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Bangaloreuniversity.jpg|thumb|235px|Bangalore University]]
J. N. Moorthy, Born  in [[B. Kothakota]], a border town in [[Chittoor district]] of the south Indian state of [[Andhra Pradesh]], graduated in chemistry from [[Bangalore University]] in 1985 and completed his master's degree from the same university in 1988.<ref name="Biodata on IITK">{{Cite web |url=http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/JNMoorthy_Vitae_Jan-2016.pdf |title=Biodata on IITK |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-date=9 October 2022 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20221009/http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/JNMoorthy_Vitae_Jan-2016.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Subsequently, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Science]] from where he secured his Phd, under the supervision of Prof. K. Venkatesan, in 1994 and went to the US to pursue his post-doctoral studies under the guidance of [[Jay Kochi]] of the [[University of Houston]]. In 1995, after obtaining an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt fellowship]], he moved to the laboratory of Waldemar Adam at the [[University of Würzburg]] where he stayed for one and half years. He subsequently moved to the [[University of Victoria]] in 1996 to work with [[Cornelia Bohne]]. In 1998, he returned to India to join the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur]] in June 1998 as an assistant professor but stayed there only for a few months and relocated to the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] where he served as an associate professor from December 2003 before becoming a professor of the department of chemistry in 2008. After holding the Lalit M. Kapoor Chair Professorship during 2011–14,<ref name="Lalit M. Kapoor Chair Professorship">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/doraold/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=79&Itemid=156 |title=Lalit M. Kapoor Chair Professorship |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220051639/http://www.iitk.ac.in/doraold/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=79&Itemid=156 |archive-date=20 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> he also served as the Dr. Jag Mohan Garg Chair Professor at the institute.<ref name="Jag Mohan Garg Chair Professorship">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitk.ac.in/doraold/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=564&Itemid=151 |title=Jag Mohan Garg Chair Professorship |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220051956/http://www.iitk.ac.in/doraold/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=564&Itemid=151 |archive-date=20 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In between, he has had various stints abroad as a visiting professor at institutions such as [[University of Bremen]] (Alexander von Humboldt fellow 2004-05), [[Jacobs University Bremen]] (Royal Society of Chemistry grants 2007), [[University of Strasburg]] (2010) and [[Osaka University]] (2010).<ref name="Biodata on IITK" /> On 1 April 2019, Professor J. N. Moorthy was appointed the Director of the [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Thiruvananthapuram]] (IISER-Thiruvananthapuram), where he served till 8 July 2026.

== Legacy ==
Moorthy received the junior and senior research fellowships (1989–93) of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, offered in association with the [[University Grants Commission of India]]<ref name="Biodata on IITK" /> and his research have been focused on the organization of organic molecules and their photoreactivity.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His contributions encompass several themes that fall into the broad ambit of ‘physical organic chemistry’. The thesis of his research has been ‘structure is an embodiment of reactivity and self-assembly’. With a diligent design of molecules and by exploiting sterics rationally, he has demonstrated control of both thermal and photochemical reactivity.<ref name="Areas of Research">{{Cite web |url=http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/Research%20Areas.html |title=Areas of Research |date=2016 |publisher=IIT Kanpur |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-date=20 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220051910/http://home.iitk.ac.in/~moorthy/Research%20Areas.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has documented his researches in several peer-reviewed articles;<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Moorthy=3AJarugu_Narasimha=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]] and [[Google Scholar]], two online repositories of scientific articles have listed >180 of them. He was on the editorial board of the International Journal of Photoenergy from 2012 to 2015 and was also been associated with the [[New Journal of Chemistry]] of the Royal Society of Chemistry as a member of its editorial board from 2011 to 2013.<ref name="Indian organic photochemist joins NJC board">{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.rsc.org/nj/2011/04/06/indian-organic-photochemist-joins-njc-board/ |title=Indian organic photochemist joins NJC board |date=2016 |publisher=New Journal of Chemistry}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Moorthy received the Young Chemist Award of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]] (CRSI) in 2003; CRSI honoured him again with the Bronze Medal in 2009.<ref name="CRSI Bronze Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-1999-2008 |title=CRSI Bronze Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Chemical Research Society of India |access-date=4 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161016123938/http://www.crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-1999-2008 |archive-date=16 October 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  In between, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2008.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=2012-09-12 }}</ref> He was elected as a fellow by the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 2010,<ref name="Fellow profile" /> Indian National Science Academy in 2018 and by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2014. The [[Indian Science Congress Association]] selected him for the Millennium Plaque of Honor in 2016.<ref name="Faculty profile" /> He has held several research fellowships including the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship]] (1995–96) and the Ramanna Fellowship (2007–10), International Centre of Trans-Disciplinary Studies (CIRET) fellowship (2008) and J. C. Bose National Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] (2015-2025).<ref name="Biodata on IITK" />
